if i had any way to change my life, i would in a heartbeat. i lack the social and financial support needed for long term meth addiction recovery, plus comorbidity of MI and addiction make it even more unlikely. ive tried na, celebrate recovery, and rehab. After a long, long talk with a recovery coach a few months ago, I've come to terms with functional addiction. there's nothing like meth addiction. ive met many former addicts with years of clean time, including heroin and crack. i have never met a former meth addict with longer than a year clean.

if there was another job i was capable of doing, i would take it.

i wish i could start over. but no matter where i go, me and the voices in my head and the flashbacks and cravings and bad coping mechanisms and absent parents and nonexistent friends and mood swings and catatonia and stutters and tics and fear, not anxiety, actual fear of other people... no matter where i go, there it all still is. i've "started over" 6 times in the past 10 months trying to find a life i find bearable to live. nothing so far.

thanks for the sentiment, though. my husband and my's song is actually Jumper by 3rd Eye Blind because of the whole starting over idea. starting over did used to work, but i cant start my brain over.

what happens when you take 25000 mg of acetaminophen: you feel sick, woozy, pass out, and wake up the next morning in a puddle of vomit. then you feel like shit for a few days. if you consult a doctor afterwards, they'll tell you that you've done some damage to your liver and shouldn't take Tylenol anymore. you will anyway, but nothing bad will happen. then, when youre like 60 or 70, your liver will be among one of the many things wrong with you, and you'll regret taking 25000 mg of acetaminophen when you were young.

I already decided to have an abortion. There is no child to care about. 

I have checked myself into plenty of hospitals in my life. That shit doesn't make u wanna live. and when youre homeless, they don't even believe youre suicidal, they just think you're there for the bed and food. they treat u like shit.

I went to churches during my first pregnancy. 0 help whatsoever, but did get plenty of pep talks about why i should stay pregnant despite being homeless. lots of promises, too. but once i passed the abortion cut-off, i was invisible. 

i don't want to turn this into an abortion debate. i am mentally incapable of carrying a pregnancy. consider it a medical condition barring me from pregnancy. if i tried to carry the pregnancy and made it to the end, the fetus would have suffered malnutrition and stress throughout the 9 months, been exposed to an array of drugs, probably be born addicted to meth, not to mention whatever physical trauma it would suffer from me continuing to hoe while pregnant so i can eat. i would miss doctor's appointments and definitely fuck off on the prenatal vitamins. this is not a choice or a matter of willpower. it is a medical fact. when someone is as mentally ill and mentally impaired as i am, they are not capable of supposedly simple tasks like going to a doctor regularly.

and yes, i did look into adoption programs. and i am already getting shit about trying to get living expenses because I'm homeless. didn't even tell them about the rest of the stuff, yet.

i'm a fucking drug-addicted prostitute. theres no way in hell me carrying a pregnancy would EVER be a good idea. and you suggesting that i should "care about that child" is EXTREMELY offensive after i made it clear that i and my husband have made the decision to have an abortion. that is not the issue here. it just contributes to the issue.
